title: NiSource Signs 20-Year Energy Supply Deal With Microsoft for Indiana Data Center
source_used: Dow Jones Newswires, read on Morningstar
key_facts: NiSource signed a long-term deal with Microsoft to provide energy for Microsoft's data centre campus in Indiana (Dow Jones Newswires).
Microsoft will begin taking electric service under a 20-year term starting in 2028, the companies said on Friday 16 Oct 2026.
The agreement is structured to serve large new customers while protecting existing Northern Indiana Public Service Company electric customers from incremental costs.
Microsoft will fully fund the generation and infrastructure required to serve its load, the companies said.

NiSource expects total savings for Northern Indiana Public Service Company electric customers of about $1.75 billion over the life of all its data-centre contracts, up from a previous projection of $1.4 billion before the Microsoft deal.
quote_evidence: NiSource has signed a long-term deal with Microsoft to provide energy for the technology company's data center campus in Indiana.
Under the agreement, Microsoft will begin taking electric service under a 20-year term starting in 2028, the companies said Friday.
As such, Microsoft will fully fund the generation and infrastructure required to serve its load, the companies said.
why_it_matters_hint: Microsoft pays for the power supply it needs, and the utility says this lowers costs for its other electricity customers.
